newsitem.title: USA: Netrix to cut workforce by 20 pct.
newsitem.headline: Netrix to cut workforce by 20 pct.

text.p: NETRIX Corp on Wednesday said it was cutting its workforce by some 20 percent and narrowing its focus as part of a drive to reduce expenses.

The company, a maker of switching products for communications networking, said in a statement the staff cuts would begin to be reflected in its second-quarter results. Lynn Chapman, who was named president and chief executive in January, announced the initiative as the company reported a decline in first-quarter revenues to $8.4 million from $11.2 million in the year-ago period. The company said the drop reflected slower sales of new products.

That resulted in a first-quarter loss of $4.6 million, or $0.48 per share, including charges of $1.4 million arising from steps taken to focus on core products. In the first quarter of last year, Netrix lost $2.3 million, or $0.25 per share, including a restructuring reserve of $900,000.
Netrix said it would concentrate on three products: the 2550, an ATM-based switch; the 2410, the next generation of the successful 1-ISS switch family; and the 2210 integrated access platform.
Company officials were not immediately available to specify how many layoffs were expected.
